approach: Fix the fault where it starts: a check killed at its deadline is stored like a real failure, so the verdict rejects the job. (1) athena.toml: check_timeout_s 900 -> 1800; config.rs untouched. (2) checks.rs: one shared `deadline_note(limit_s)` used by `run_check` and by the classifier `timed_out(&CheckRun)`, and `held_for_timeout(&[CheckRun], Option<&Baseline>)`. It looks only at NEW failures (failed and not `verify::is_pre_existing` against the baseline `check_and_verify` already passes to `mark_pre_existing`) and returns Some only when there is at least one new failure and every new failure timed out. (3) disk.rs: `CHECK_TIMEOUT = "environment: check timed out"`, a reason builder with measured duration and limit, and `is_environment_reason` accepts it, so `resumable_stop` and the resume marks follow unchanged. (4) run/mod.rs `check_and_verify`: when checks were not resumed and `held_for_timeout` is Some, close with `self.failure(..)` before the verifier, as the low-disk stop does; otherwise today's path (including rejection) is unchanged. A cfg(test) fake-check seam lives inside run/mod.rs and is read first in `SnapExec::exec`. (5) status.rs: `CheckDurations` (median, slowest, count, limit, 80% flag) over the newest 20 request jobs, counting only `test` runs that actually ran (skips 'not run' placeholders and entries with no measured value). (6) display.rs: one `if let` printing that text in `athena status`. (7) CHANGELOG entry citing 20261026-232434-6wfq.

decisions.choice: Classify a timeout by exit_code None plus the shared deadline note (`timed_out`), the note text built by one function (`deadline_note`) used by both `run_check` and the classifier.
decisions.reason: CheckRun gains no field (out of scope). One function for the text means writer and reader cannot drift. `mark_pre_existing` only prefixes the note, so a 'contains' match still classifies correctly after marking. The kill-switch note and the 'ran zero tests' note differ, so they are not read as timeouts.

rejected.why: Out of scope; changes the record schema and AnyRecord handling.

rejected.option: Match 'killed at the deadline' separately in run/mod.rs
rejected.why: A duplicated string that can drift from checks.rs.

decisions.choice: Round 2 finding 2 (pre-existing failures): `held_for_timeout(checks, baseline)` considers only new failures, `!c.passed && !verify::is_pre_existing(c, baseline)`. It holds when that set is non-empty and every member is `timed_out`. `check_and_verify` passes `usable_baseline`, the same value it gives `mark_pre_existing`, and calls it after `mark_pre_existing`.
decisions.reason: `judge` passes a job whose only failures are pre-existing, so ignoring the baseline would turn a job that passes today into an environment stop that fails the same way on every retry when the test check also timed out on the base (case a). A pre-existing real failure beside a new timeout must not count as a real failure of this job, or the timeout would cause a rejection (case b). `is_pre_existing` depends only on `passed` and the baseline, not the note, so calling it after marking is safe. Four cases follow: a pre-existing timeout alone is not held (the job goes to the verifier and passes as today); a pre-existing real failure plus a new timeout is held; a pre-existing timeout plus a new real failure is not held (rejected); a new timeout plus a new real failure is not held (rejected).

rejected.option: Hold when every failed check timed out, ignoring the baseline (the round 1 plan)
rejected.why: Gets cases (a) and (b) wrong, as the critic showed.

rejected.option: Hold whenever any check timed out
rejected.why: Would let a real failure be retried away instead of rejected.

rejected.option: Put the baseline filtering in the caller in run/mod.rs
rejected.why: Splits one rule across two files; the unit cases are easier to show on one pure function.

decisions.choice: Reason prefix `environment: check timed out`, recognised in `is_environment_reason`.
decisions.reason: It starts with scope_guard's ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX. `resumable_stop` and `settle_resume_marks` already key on `is_environment_reason`, so `athena retry` resumes from the kept candidate with no other change.

rejected.why: Schema change; the Failed + environment-reason mechanism already exists.

decisions.choice: The cfg(test) seam module `check_seam` is defined inside run/mod.rs next to its only reader `SnapExec::exec` (run/mod.rs around line 969), in the shape of `replay_seam` (thread-local Option<Rc<dyn Fn(&CheckSpec) -> CheckRun>>, install returning a Drop guard, current). `SnapExec::exec` is the Exec that `routing::run_local` calls for every local check, so the seam replaces only the process run.
decisions.reason: Classification, reason building, closing and state stay in production code; the thread-local keeps parallel tests isolated; lib.rs is not touched (round 1 finding 2).

rejected.why: It would sit in the very function whose kill behaviour is classified; the fake would replace the code under test.

rejected.option: A real sleep with a 1 s limit
rejected.why: Gives '1s of 1s limit', adds the 5 s kill grace, no exact duration. The real-kill assertion of `timed_out` stays in checks.rs.

decisions.choice: Round 2 finding 4: the mixed timeout-plus-real-failure case is shown at `held_for_timeout` outright, with no conditional job-level test.
decisions.reason: `routing::run_local` stops at the first failed check, so a local run never yields a mixed set; one arises only from CI-reused records. `held_for_timeout` is the function `check_and_verify` calls, so a unit test on it exercises production code. The job-level contrast is the real nonzero exit rejected (criterion 3) against the timeout held (criterion 2), both through `Athena::go`.

rejected.option: A job test with a two-check capability, added if the harness supports it
rejected.why: Conditional, and it cannot reach a mixed set through local runs anyway.

decisions.choice: Round 2 finding 1 (display.rs): keep the few-line edit to crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs `status()` (line 957), the only code that prints StatusView (called from main.rs line 1210). All logic and the text stay in status.rs.
decisions.reason: Criterion 5 and the reading require `athena status` to print the report. I searched crates/athena-cli/src: no other printer exists, and the reading's list names status.rs but omits the file that prints it. Without the edit the report exists only in `status --json`. It is not a governance file. If the scope check refuses it, the producer stops and reports rather than hiding the report in another printed field.

rejected.why: Those fields mean an action, a build warning and the bootstrap state; mislabelling a report to dodge a file boundary is a workaround.

decisions.choice: Round 2 finding 3 (status durations): `check_durations` reads the newest 20 `Records::request_jobs()` (already sorted newest first) through one private helper `test_check_seconds(&JobRecords) -> Option<f64>` in status.rs. The helper takes the check named `test` from `verification.checks` and counts it only when `duration.value()` is Some and `duration.basis() != "not run"`. Skipped runs (`checks::skipped_run`, basis 'not run') and nested placeholders (run/mod.rs line 1423, basis 'not run') are therefore excluded. Jobs with no counted run are skipped, and the 20-job window counts jobs that qualify.
decisions.reason: The 0 s placeholders would pull the median down and hide a near-limit trend. Median of an even count is the mean of the two middle values; flag = slowest > 0.8 x limit; the limit is the configured check_timeout_s.

rejected.option: Edit code_health::suite_seconds to share the helper
rejected.why: code_health.rs is not a deliverable. I read it: `suite_seconds` returns only the latest test duration and also counts a 0 s 'not run' entry. The producer should not change it here; the fault and a one-line fix (apply the same basis filter) go to open_questions.

rejected.option: Parse durations out of closing reasons
rejected.why: Fragile text parsing, and still no check record for held jobs.
Includes 0 s placeholders, as the critic found.

decisions.reason: No config rewriting in the test; the printed limit is shown to come from the real configured value.

risks.risk: A genuinely hung check is held as an environment stop and never rejected.
risks.mitigation: The stop is a Failed job that needs a manual `athena retry`, not an automatic loop. The reason names the check, duration and limit, and `athena status` flags near-limit checks at 80%.

risks.risk: The fake could hide a wrong classification.
risks.mitigation: The fake supplies only a CheckRun whose note comes from the shared `checks::deadline_note`; a checks.rs test uses a real `run_check` kill to show `timed_out` is true for a real kill. Classification and closing run in production code.

risks.risk: A baseline that is unusable (wrong base commit, or a note set) makes `is_pre_existing` false, so a timeout that also happens on the base is held as new.
risks.mitigation: This matches how `judge` treats the same baseline, so hold and verdict agree. `check_and_verify` passes only `usable_baseline`, the base-commit-matched value. A hold writes no results, so a retry reruns the checks.

risks.risk: Adding a StatusView field breaks other constructors or JSON expectations.
risks.mitigation: The only StatusView literal is in `status()` (status.rs around line 1311). The field is skipped in JSON when None. fmt, clippy and the full test run cover the rest.

risks.risk: The scope check refuses display.rs, which is not a listed deliverable.
risks.mitigation: The edit is a few lines and is named with its reason. No workaround through other printed fields is planned; if refused, the producer stops and reports.

risks.risk: A held job writes no check record, so its duration never enters the status report; the jobs closest to the limit are the most likely to be missing.
risks.mitigation: Accepted per the reading and the low-disk precedent; the closing reason carries duration and limit. A later change could record the check run.

risks.risk: The resume mark for a held job stays at stage Checks, so a retry reruns all checks.
risks.mitigation: Intended: no passing results exist to reuse. `settle_resume_marks` keeps the mark for environment reasons, so the retry skips the planner and producer.

risks.risk: The status helper and `code_health::suite_seconds` read the same data in two places.
risks.mitigation: Kept to one helper inside the deliverables (status.rs); the unchanged `suite_seconds` is named in open_questions with its one-line fix.

demonstrations.method: Job-level test `a_check_killed_at_its_deadline_closes_as_an_environment_stop` in `produce_and_verify_order_tests` (crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs). Entry point: `Athena::go` on a job from `athena.ask(..)` in the existing harness (`athena_with`, `Docs` capability, fake agent script, `repo()` loading athena.toml). Preconditions: `test_support::plenty_of_space`, checks not resumed, not nested, no usable baseline. Seam: `check_seam::install(..)`, a cfg(test) module that step 4 adds to run/mod.rs (it does not exist today; modelled on `replay_seam` in lib.rs, which exists), read in `SnapExec::exec` (exists, around line 969). The fake returns only a CheckRun with exit_code None, passed false, note `checks::deadline_note(1800)` and duration 1805 s. `held_for_timeout`, the reason builder, `failure` and the state come from production code, not the fake.
demonstrations.observes: The job closes Failed (not Rejected); `disk::is_environment_reason(&reason)` is true; `disk::resumable_stop(JobState::Closed(Failed), Some(&reason))` is true; the verifier call counter is 0.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the `held_for_timeout` early return the job goes on to the verifier, `judge` sees a failed check and the state is Rejected, so the Failed, environment and resumable assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Three parts. (a) Job-level `a_real_nonzero_check_failure_is_still_rejected` through `Athena::go` with no seam installed: the real `run_check` runs a capability check `false` (a real exit 1). (b) Unit test `held_for_timeout_needs_a_new_failure_and_every_new_failure_timed_out` in checks.rs, calling `held_for_timeout`, the function `check_and_verify` calls, on seeded CheckRun values (pure records, no seam; `Baseline` literals use its public fields, with note None). The mixed case is shown here outright because `run_local` stops at the first failure. Cases: [timeout, exit 1] and [exit 1, timeout] give None (these are the rejected 'one timed out, another failed for real' sets); [timeout] gives Some; all-pass gives None; a failure with the kill-switch note gives None; pre-existing timeout alone (baseline failed `test`) gives None; pre-existing real failure plus new timeout gives Some; pre-existing timeout plus new real failure gives None. (c) A real-kill test `a_real_deadline_kill_is_classified_as_a_timeout` in checks.rs runs `run_check` with a 300 ms limit (as the existing baseline timeout test does) and asserts `timed_out`, so the shared note is shown to match a real kill.
demonstrations.observes: A real nonzero exit leaves the job Rejected with a non-environment reason; every set containing a new real failure is not held (so judge rejects it as today); pre-existing failures never cause a hold or a rejection by themselves; a real kill is classified as a timeout.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the hold ignored real failures, the mixed cases would return Some and a real failure would be retried instead of rejected. If it ignored the baseline, the pre-existing timeout alone would return Some (a passing job turned into a failing stop) and the pre-existing failure plus new timeout case would return None.

demonstrations.method: Pure unit test in disk.rs `check_timeout_reason_names_the_duration_and_the_limit` calling `check_timeout_reason("test", 905, 900, job)`, plus the criterion 2 job test, which reads the stored closing reason and the printed line from the harness `Lines` UI. Seam as in criterion 2.
demonstrations.observes: The unit test finds `905s of 900s limit` and `athena retry` in the reason. The job test finds `1805s of 1800s limit` in both the stored closing reason and the printed `failed     ` line, the limit coming from `jc.config.budget.check_timeout_s` as loaded from athena.toml.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the reason omitted the duration or the limit, or used another format, the `905s of 900s limit` and `1805s of 1800s limit` substring assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Tests in status.rs on `check_durations(&Records, limit_s)` and `CheckDurations::text()`, the functions `Athena::status()` calls to fill `StatusView.check_durations`; fixture: `Records` seeded like the existing status.rs tests that seed `verification`. Seed 22 request jobs, each with a `test` check of a chosen measured duration (basis 'measured'); the oldest 2 have huge durations to show only the newest 20 count; one job has no `test` check (skipped); one newest job has a skipped/placeholder `test` entry (0 s, basis 'not run') to show it is excluded from both the count and the median. Case A: slowest 1500 s of 1800 gives flagged true and text with median, slowest and limit. Case B: slowest 1000 s gives no flag. Case C: exactly 1440 s (80%) is not flagged. A display.rs test `status_prints_the_check_durations_line` calls `display::status` and asserts the line is printed when `check_durations` is Some and absent when None (it builds the view with the same helper the existing display status tests use, if one exists; otherwise it takes a view from a seeded `Athena::status()`).
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-core check_durations_report_median_slowest_and_the_eighty_percent_flag && cargo test --locked -p athena-cli status_prints_the_check_durations_line
demonstrations.observes: The text shows median and slowest test-check durations over the last 20 jobs against the limit, flagged exactly when slowest exceeds 80% of the limit; the 'not run' placeholder does not lower the median or count as a job; `athena status` output contains the line.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the computation there is no line. With a window of all jobs the median and slowest differ from the expected values. With a wrong threshold, case B or C flips. If 'not run' placeholders were counted, the seeded median would be lower than expected. Without the display edit the display test finds no line.

demonstrations.method: Content check: Grep `CHECK_TIMEOUT` in crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs to see `is_environment_reason` contains `reason.starts_with(CHECK_TIMEOUT)`. Unit test `the_check_timeout_reason_is_an_environment_reason` in the disk.rs tests module. Pure functions, no seam.
